newsitem.title: USA: Fireman's Fund to acquire Crop Growers.
newsitem.headline: Fireman's Fund to acquire Crop Growers.

text.p: Fireman's Fund Insurance Co and Crop Growers Corp said Thursday they had agreed for Fireman's Fund to acquire Crop Growers for $10.25 a share.

Fireman's Fund presently owns convertible preferred stock of Crop Growers and has exercised the right to purchase 1.8 million common shares from former Crop Growers executives at $10 a share, the companies said in a joint statement.
The transaction is subject to, among other things, Crop Growers stockholder approval, regulatory approval and other customary conditions, they said.
The deal is not expected to close for several months due to regulatory approvals and clearances, the companies said.

The terms of the transaction have been unanimously approved by Crop Growers's board, which has received an opinion from financial adviser Dean Witter Reynolds that the deal is fair to Crop Growers stockholders, the companies said.

Crop Growers, which has about eight million shares outstanding, is allowed to seek other acquisition offers from certain companies and may receive unsolicited bids through March 28, the companies said.
If Crop Growers receives a better offer, it could terminate the deal with Fireman's Fund upon payment of a $2.4 million break-up fee, they said.
After March 28, Crop Growers may terminate the deal under more limited circumstances, they said.
Fireman's Fund is a wholly owned subsidiary of Allianz AG Holding of Germany.
